item.title: Uncool puppets (needs greenlit)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A pair of sock puppets possessed by their creator who tried to be part of AWCY but accidentally ended up being stuck in two socks.

Central Narrative: A middle-aged woman attempted to use her minor reality warping powers to impress the GOI Are We Cool Yet by creating an army of living sock puppets. This went wrong and her consciousness was placed in two sock puppets. She is mostly well adapted to her situation and is basically harmless. She only complains in containment when individuals attempt to wear her.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is an odd object with a funny story behind it, but is not just a joke. There's a vast number of potential futures for these socks that can be shown properly with someone much better than I at emotional writing.

Additional Notes: This is a small SCP to balance out the gods and cosmic powers that seem to be filling containment. There is nothing wrong with that, but maybe we need more socks in cells.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Keep Him In The Dark
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

A number of incident logs in which he realizes that the world around him has changed, and warps reality to change it back.

So like, what do these actually look like? My concern is that you're in a situation where they don't add a lot individually but they're also not really hugely interesting; and so you both want short logs to not dwell on them much but also longer logs to really try and show why they are interesting; and neither option quite works.

culminating in an interview in which he is finally informed of his abilities, and chooses to assist the foundation in making sure he is unaware of when he shifts, especially after reflecting on the harm he's caused.

so like, this is fine but like…if he realises he's caused a lot of harm, and there's implication he's in full control of his reality bending abilities, why does he need to be kept unaware of when shifts occur? Surely he can just like…understand that is what is going on and not get mad?

More to the point, why does he even alter reality? Like I get him wanting to shift stuff back towards what it should be on paper but it doesn't seem like there's any changes that actually materially affect him since he's in foundation containment in all the cases and there's not like a big driving force like "my wife died in 6/7 of the realities and i want her to be around still"?

I think my big concern is that the narrative arc feels excessively shallow and very late: the actual growth of the SCP doesn't kick in until the final act when he's told about the reality bending powers and then it immediately all happens then; and it feels like the earlier incident logs just…are filler material to bridge the gap instead of like, actually adding to what you want to do here?

item.title: Re: A Multiversal Joyride
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I think my biggest concern with this pitch is that it feels very passive in terms of the role of the Foundation here: bear in mind, your PoV for telling this story as a SCP is the Foundation and their researchers. Which in turn means that if you write a story that's entirely about the backstory of entity 1, and them falling in love and the love falling apart and causing them a lot of emotional pain, the reader will be separated from all this emotional both temporally (in that, all of this has happened already, in the past) and narratively (in that, we can't experience the emotional reaction first hand, and instead rely on the entity telling us this, or the foundation piecing this together via some other medium).

On some level, I'm kinda confused about what the actual…plot beats are here? There's a lot of stuff that's very briefly mentioned and I don't really have a good idea for what the overall narrative looks like, or how you're intending to convey it: like, is this gonna be told via diary entries from the entity? Interviews? MTF teams being sent to the alternate reality and piecing together what happened there?

The basic idea is a machine from another reality crashing on earth by accident.

I'm always pretty iffy about stuff like this because space is very big and very empty and the chance of a space ship crashing on earth is astronomically low; and so it just always feels very convenient when it does happen.

item.title: Prince Charming
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Speech: SCP- XXXX is a young man that has an unnatural hair and eye color that changes depending on his mood, with a short height, an unnatural pale skin and mostly of all, has an unworldly charisma. He wears a crown and clothes of a prince like those in fairytales indicating that he's from another world or the era where royals exists (I'm still looking for what that era or time was called). SCP-XXXX shows no sign of aging and has an ungodly regenaration ability but most of all his presence makes people love him romantically despite their gender, but being expose to XXXX longer makes them more love him and more exposure can make people be obsessed with him and makes people fight to death for his love and for more longer exposure, it can make them crazy and insane, deeming themselves not worthy of XXXX's love and commits suicide, though the worst part is the dead body of the people that surrounds XXXX turned to smoke which XXXX absorbs enhancing his regenerative ability.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX was found wandering around the forest of one of the facilities of the SCP Foundation with confusion and sadness written on his face and hair that keeps turning to yellow and blue. The personnels that was guarding the perimeter of the said facility, find it weird and interesting at the same time, and without hesitation quickly implemented an order to quickly capture him.

They quickly send out a team to capture him, though upon contact the agents stopped and examine XXXX intently. XXXX quickly introduced himself with a smile as Prince Jun, his hair and eye color turning in a bright yellow, the agents dropped their weapons, going on their knees and bows towards him.

Meanwhile, The researchers that was watching from the CCTV cameras find it odd and interesting, and continued to watch what would happen. And from the footage they saw that all of the agents are kissing XXXX hands before they quickly stand up and leads him towards the SCP Facility, but before they can reach the gates all the agents started to act weird, first it started by bickering, to arguing, but the last is the most unexpected as the agents out of nowhere started killing each other while XXXX just continue to walk towards the gates without batting an eye.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Find out what is in store for this prince (Its all I can think of at the moment, since this is my first project)
.

Additional Notes: This is my first idea, I'm new in here and I want to know what you guys think about it, also I was suppose to make this guy a creepypasta but I changed my mind.

item.title: Re: SCP: The Tooth Jar (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

True, I felt like I had to pitch in logs, since you seemed to want a more story-telling article, but they actually won't add much.

Yes; I generally like scp articles which are more like short stories than encyclopedia entries on a weird thing; or at least, articles which do something with the weird thing to really evoke an emotion, y'know? Just describing the article won't cut it for me; but 'for me' and 'for everyone on the site' don't necessarily mix and you're welcome to ask other folk.

My concern is if 'they actually won't add much', why add them at all? The entire point of me pushing you towards something more narratively driven here is to force you to come up with a way to show why this is interesting and not just describe a weird thing; and adding elements that aren't adding to that doesn't help.

It's only a small detail. It would be hypothetized in the article that this is linked to the transmutation, which happens at the atomic stage.

this doesn't make me feel less like you tacked the radioactivity on to make it seem more interesting.

I see what you mean. I didn't think all SCPs required a horryfing bit.

I mean, they don't; it's just, when you have these elements, it feels like the easiest emotion to create here is a gross 'i ate a spoonful of rice and it turned into a thousand teeth' kinda vibe.

I guess really what I was getting at here is "it feels like this needs a bit where it all comes together to imply something bigger; whether it's a horrifying moment at the end like in salsa hammer where you realise it doesn't kill people initially; or a cathartic moment like in SCP-091 where you realise the tissue box provides comfort to people or something else, y'know?

item.title: Re: SCP - The God Killer
item.content:encoded:
No worries; keep in mind I'm not an official critter, so take what I said with a grain of salt. Regarding the similarity to God of War, it's not necessarily a bad thing if you can put your own spin on it (and it's well written). Regarding the Mary-Sue comment, I was referring to the fact that the entity is near-indestructible; there's already a lot of articles like that on the site, so it comes across a little cliché. Just an idea, but maybe he was much stronger in his original dimension, but in the ours, he's less formidable? But again, this is all just my opinion; if you can pull off a near-indestructible demigod, go for it!

I'm not sure if you know, but posters are typically expected to contact seasoned critters from The Butterfly Squad for feedback. So look through the list, see who'd be most suited to give you feedback, and send off a couple of WikiDot PMs. Alternatively, you can contact people in the IRC Chat. If you don't contact anyone, you might be waiting a while before someone authorised to give greenlights will come along.

Good luck with your article!

item.title: Re: The Midas Brick
item.content:encoded:
Hey there DrGreywhind, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither a particularly experienced nor an offical reviewer, so take everything I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Thoughts +
*sparkly noises*

I'd like to start off by assuring you that SCPs don't have to be an immediate threat to humanity, the world, or reality itself (in fact, almost all of them aren't). A non-dangerous Safe-class SCP has just as much potential to be interesting, if not moreso, than some super-deadly Keter.

Next, I'd like to address your idea. I agree with Zaihan that the idea is underwhelming, but for different reasons. Firstly, it's not very original (as you said, it shares many similarities with SCP-409, and also SCP-1015). In fact, it is almost a clone of both mentioned SCPs in that it transmutes the people (or objects) it touches into the material it consists of.

Secondly, the backstory implies the existence of Kind Midas at some point (despite his status as a mythological figure) and also that the brick's existence was covered up somehow (despite it turning everything to gold). These are both pretty hefty logical issues which I'd like for you to fix.

I'd recommend 2 things:
1. Checking out the Guide Hub for some great essays on stuff like ideation and story-ing!
2. Contacting some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad. They've got tonnes of experience and are quite helpful!

And finally, to sum up your idea in one sentence1:
A golden block of wood (the first thing Midas touched) gained his abilities.


Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!
Footnotes
1. This is to help you get an idea of the bare bones of what a critter sees when they read your summary. You may find something here that you don't like, or realise we're getting the wrong impression.

Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The Midas Brick

Thanks for the read, the vote and most importantly by far, the comment.

+ Thoughts!
- Begone, thoughts!

I agree that this piece takes a hit from the fact that it's being written by someone who can't provide an indigenous perspective, won't try to puppeteer one, and won't change his approach to suit what he can provide. That was pretty much intentional; the only way I knew how to tell the story about cultural appropriation I wanted to tell was to tread the line, just as you describe, and hope that the message that came through worked well enough for most people to make it worthwhile.

Ideally, someone who actually is from the related cultures would see this, and be interested in providing the missing perspective themselves in their writing. I would love to see people who have actual experience with the subject matter writing about it, whether in completely original form or making use of this piece as a springboard if necessary. Barring that, this will stand as my imperfect but hopefully not valueless intervention on the issues. I wouldn't have done it at all, except that I imagined someone taking this mythological creature and writing a bog-standard horror tale using it. This was my attempt to head that off at the pass.

I don't intend to write anything further on a wholly indigenous topic, and was very leery about writing this one; I had some angry points I wanted to make, though, so I made them and hoped that my intent would shine through. It seems to have.

I very much appreciate your taking the time to dissect what I wrote, and am 100% on the same page with you about the results (although I probably like it more than you do :P) The next SCP I wrote, SCP-5520, was an oblique take on something I had personal experience with… though, it turns out, not as personal as one of my readers.

item.title: Re: SCP that preys on sex predators (Trigger Warning: Description of an Abuser and his crimes)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback

Response
Response

I see what you my wording might be confusing with regards to the lack of identity. What I meant to express is that the SCP shapeshifts into a person that is very attractive to the target in order to lure them. The SCP was basically being confused for multiple different people by the police investigators. The SCP isn't removing the targets from reality, the corpses are very much still there after the murder.

The use of sexual predators as victims wasn't meant to be a cheap attempt for shock value. What I want to do is use the murder's of sexual predators to explore the morality behind killing those who we deem evil. Although the death penalty is outlawed in my country the same can't be said for the rest of the world, like countries such as the US where the story takes place. So by seeing the murder of sexual predators from the perspective of an unapologetically hateful killer. The violence serves the purpose of elevating the hypothetical killing of "evil people" in the real world to a fictional exageratted scenario to highlight how death for anyone is an awful thing to experience. Again not for shock value but to relate back to the central question of "do evil people deserve death?"

I do agree the way I described the SCP as a "vicious and psychotic beast" was not accurate to how I want to portray. I think a more accurate description of what I have imagined is hateful, apathetic and sadistic. I want the creature to be symbolic of the feeling you get when you hear about an evil person doing something awful. That burst of hatred that makes you clench your fists and jaw, maybe slam a desk or wall. I want that feeling embodied in a physical form by this creature. As the creature is meant to represent an extension of an aspect of human psychology I think it makes sense to give it humanlike psychology. As for it's reasoning behind why it hunts predators I think giving it a logical and reasonable justification for killing would contadict it's symbolism of human hatred. When it comes to human psychology it is often anything but logical. People feel the way they feel often regardless of what makes sense, when you're in a state of hatred like that it's hard to stop and think about the moral implications of murdering a sex offender you just let the hate burn until you calm down. So "psychotic" describes the mental state of the SCP during it's kill; agressive, hyperactive, hostile and lack of restraint. All symptoms of psychosis.

Obviously I can't explain all of this in 400 words so I apologise if I wasn't able to convey exactly what I meant in my pitch. I just wanted to explain my idea better before you judge it as cliche and boring shock value content. Your feedback did help me realize however that I need to express the ideas above better in my Idea Pitch so I'll try to rewrite it so it can do so. Thank you for that. I know my idea isn't perfect but I am commited to making it the best version of itself that I can.

item.title: Re: Perfectly parallel (green light wanted)
item.content:encoded:
Alright, this idea has merit, but there are some points I would like to address.

uwu
OWO oh no u woke him up!

I'm gonna point out some things I view as flaws before moving to the promising bits.

Compulsion Affects:
In most cases, having an anomalous effect that forces somebody to do something or act in a certain way is a lazy writing strategy. The same effect you're trying to achieve can be done without any kind of cognitohazard or compulsion. For example, they recently found a metal monolith in the Utah desert and somebody on Reddit already found where it is, despite its sheer remoteness. Realistically, only one person needs to find the pole and post it online and the following will grow organically as more curious people try to find it.

As for the pole, as you said, the symmetry could be extremely enchanting to only some people, which would be a great in for the Foundation, as the news reports on people refusing to leave the structure.

Beyond my nitpick regarding compulsion, you're gonna need a strong enough story via the Foundation agent to carry the article or it'll just be another "weird object that kills you." Perhaps they slowly begin to uncover more about the origin of the poles because they aren't really affected by the poles.

All and all, I think it has merit, but I do want to see that you avoid the pitfalls of early SCP writing.

item.title: The God Killer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Small bit of Horror, Drama/Emotional, bit of Action, some History

Page Layout (Optional): Standard Description and Containment Procedures, interview, discovery log, and requests.

Elevator Pitch: it is basically a man that can change his size to anything he wants, is completely invincable and unstoppable. (except for the gases that the foundation make) he was originally made to kill gods and devour them. shredding them down to their atoms. but he gets betrayed by the humans and sent to the SCP universe.

Central Narrative: the basic idea of this, is that the SCP is from another universe. in that universe the main mythology gods and deities exist (like Odin and Zeus) each one basically owning a portion of the world (like the olympians getting Greece and the Egyptians getting Egypt) and making it their own. but after millions of years of the gods and other smaller deities ruling the world. the humans become fed up. they combine magic and science to create SCP-XXXX (no number) this entity is made to destroy these “gods” one by one and free man kind. but little do they know that with every god, deity and demi-god it kills it gains a little bit of humanity. eventually after killing and devouring every last god, it has become essentially human in emotions. but when it returns and is told the kill code, it lives and realises that they tried to kill him after all it did for them. It begins to attack the humans, but they open a wormhole and it is sent to the scp universe, where he gets contained and evetually stored.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: whats special about this idea is that we get to see the building of a god from another world. and after he learns about being human he instantly doesn't want to be one because of what his people did to him. so it's like a betrayal story that makes people feel empathy for him, then sadness as he gets betrayed again in the SCP universe.

Additional Notes: i would love this idea to reach draft status, as i have had this idea for a novel for a long time and i thought it would be great to get feedback from here. and if it became and scp. it would make a great story character to have in many different stories.
anyway im blabbering too much and i really thank you for reading my idea! :)

item.title: Re: Electricity
item.content:encoded:
I don't really have much to add here that isn't very similar to what the other people here are saying.

Your idea isn't exactly an original one on the Site, as Grigori Karpin pointed out, and to back up their point, allow me to point you to this article: the Second Second Law of Thermodynamics. Other than the primary anomaly (and some differences in story), your idea is almost exactly the same as that one.

I'd suggest finding something to differentiate your idea from SCP-4039. If you can't or won't, I'd personally recommend scrapping this idea due to how difficult it would be to execute it successfully without looking like a clone of the aforementioned SCP.

I'd also suggest checking out the Guide Hub for some great essays on ideation, narrative writing/structure, and much more!

Anyway, that's it for my crit. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps.

i'm conflicted about this. prose is good, concept is good, formatting is good. but this work is *political* and that means i can analyse the *politics*.

+ so here's the thing
- if you care to read

you nailed the tone, and how a work like this really ought to go… in addendum 2. the rest felt kind of off.

basically this handled the message of "racism against first nations is bad" way better than the complicated matter of genuine colonialism.

the former was crystal clear. incompetent and racist government, huge anti-indigenous sentiment, the foundation being ignorant but otherwise impartial. i'm also going to go against the grain and say that scout's final message was actually good, and worked in-universe.

the latter… was messy. i got it, but it was messy. the expropriation of land (which happened, but they made up for it by helping those who were persecuted), listening to indigenous voices (which you are not, i am not, and of which there were none in the work), cultural appropriation (i don't think this work is that, but you and i both know it's mighty fucking close).

it's hard to mix that tight-rope with a feel-good story about overcoming ignorance, helping first nations people, respecting culture, etc.

i frankly don't think you pulled that aspect off. not bad, but only good. it's fundamentally a story about two important named scientists with lives and histories, and The Natives Of The Region. that's fair. you are only really able to tell the parts of the story here that are yours to tell. that makes it weak, but it's not strictly your fault. you're self-aware based on your other comments, too, which is good.

i am curious to see what you do next, and how your social commentary matures, especially if you venture into matters which you are more personally familiar with.

overall though, this was above average in all other regards. +1

item.title: Re: Living on repeat
item.content:encoded:
The idea is that every death will trigger a new set of logs, as every trip through is slightly different. Through this process, you are going to see the effect of living multiple lifetimes in Foundation custody

Well this already doesn't make sense, as they wouldn't have records of the past lives. Either it didn't happen at all or this is an alternative universe.

  • What does containment even look like for this man? How would the Foundation do anything about this? If you mean just trying to keep him alive, that's horribly passive containment.
  • What evidence would the Foundation even have of an anomaly?
  • More importantly tho, why would he need to be contained? He's not really a threat to the Veil.

Narratively I still think this is a bit weak, there's little stakes for the Foundation to get involved or the reader to get invested. Dude is gonna live again anyway, right?

Also… and I don't wanna ask the obvious, but what sets this apart from like Groundhog Day, and every other timeloop thing? Just that he lives his whole life?

item.title: Re: Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded:
What would, to you, satisfy that definition of unpredictable/novel material?

Something along the lines of a quirky or unusual motivation behind the existence of the sanitarium, which would catch the audience off-guard if they're expecting a typical horror genre setup. SCP-2662, for example, is a great subversion of the typical cult-drawing otherworldly terror entity in that it doesn't want people to worship it, and also feels extremely uncomfortable when people do. The dialogue and behaviors/mannerisms of the entity flesh out the character in a meaningful, believable way. You can also look at the discussion thread for that article to see what readers specifically liked about the characterization.

And what is, "that's just what they do"? Is it the lack of explanation into what the sanitorium is/does that is dissatisfied?

No, I would need to know more about why the sanitarium does what it does. Though in all honesty, the "what" it does also needs some work because it's pretty predictable so far as horror genre material goes.

How is this a generic monster and what would you recommend to improve it? I still plan to pursue this entity even if it never finds its way into a published article. So what can be done to make it unique?

It's a generic monster in that it has powers and harms people and has no personality or relatable features. So far as improvement goes, it depends on how you as the author want the audience to respond to the entity. With fear? Pity? Intrigue?

Finally, is it possible to make an SCP tale without a corresponding article?

Yes. We have a lot of tales based on anomalies that aren't mainlisted.

item.title: Modern Day Soldier
item.content:encoded:
First SCP idea. An entity that takes the form of a soldier. This soldier has exceptional skills in hand-to-hand combat and use of modern day weaponry.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes!

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: My SCP idea is an entity that takes a form of a soldier (pretty much a U.S Soldier).

  • Has a unique form that make him invulnerable to most damage (mainly being bullets, his form weakens by any sort of explosives)
  • Has weapons that are connected to him and cannot be removed (if someone attempts to, the soldier gets irritated and even aggressive)
  • The soldier entity gets PTSD an effect that resembles PTSD, while in this state, he goes berserk, destroying everything he sees in a fit of rage.
  • Can communicate with humans in mainly English
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: This SCP is an unknown entity that takes the form of a soldier. No one knows exactly what the entity is or why it's taking the form of a soldier, but theories are that the entity was released from an unknown containment in an anonymous operation led by the U.S Government. This SCP is an excellent hand-to-hand fighter, shooter, and uses military strategies. This SCP is also known to be relatively peaceful (as it is a soldier), but can be violent if angered, or in the state of his PTSD effect. The U.S Government insists that they know nothing of the soldier, but some scientists think they are lying. SCP officials think that the soldier was once a leader of the squad with how he talks and uses his strategies of moving through buildings/locations and how secretive he is in interviews. The form of this SCP is unknown to SCP officials as it's an unusual substance and can make the wearer immune to most damage. This SCP is known to get out of containment easily when angered by officials or D-Class, but seems blind when in it's PTSD effect.

Hook/Attention-Grabbers: I find this idea for an SCP to be unique because you don't see a lot of humanoid SCPs with actual guns. I find that what's best about SCPs is the mystery around them; like where they come from and what the goals of the SCPs are. This idea has a bit of mystery of who the soldier is, what the form substance could be, and I will probably add more mysteries to this SCP if I am able to write about it.

The overall concepts that I think makes this idea unique: An SCP who uses modern day weapons to dispatch enemies, the mystery of this SCP, and that it's a soldier SCP.

Additional Notes: NONE.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Your Friendly Neighbourhood Thermonuclear Bomb
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: A cardboard standee for a nuclear bomb informational evening come to life. Displays all signs of an activated thermonuclear weapon. 1950's-60's sociable. Invites people to dinner to inform them of the benefits of thermonuclear weapons.

Central Narrative: "The Bomb" is sapient and sentient cardboard cutout of a thermonuclear missile, with limbs attached via twist-pins. Despite being made of cardboard and rudimentary electronics causing it's actuation, it displays the exact same properties as a live thermonuclear bomb. It's purpose is to talk to and convince it's "neighbors" (read: any sapient/sentient object nearby) of the many uses and benefits of thermonuclear weaponry. Has a very 1950's-60's "idyllic" nuclear home outlook. Will try to invite it's "neighbors" over for barbecue dinners, where, nearing the end of the dinner, continuing it's idealization of thermonuclear weapons. it will produce potato salad wherein the potatoes have been baked via thermonuclear detonation (edible, but probably not healthy). Found near Nye County, Nevada, reports it was "clear to be activated" when a disgruntled nuclear information evening worker dumped potato salad on the electronics causing it to move and speak.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Creepy insistence on the benefit of thermonuclear weaponry to an almost absurd degree. 1950's-60's delusion. Potato salad.

Additional Notes: Please do not attempt to ride the cardboard cut-out with a cowboy hat. We tried, and it did not appreciate it.
